scopeNote: The public list contains only source-stated conjectures, open questions, limitations, extensions, and status updates.

openItems.title: Optimality of the fixed non-stockout-probability policy
openItems.statement: For the classical periodic-review lost-sales model with linear holding and penalty costs and continuous demand, the paper conjectures that the FP3 policy whose target satisfies its optimality equation is optimal.
openItems.paperEstablishes: The paper derives an optimality equation, develops an FP3 policy and its approximation, and reports numerical comparisons. Its long-lead-time discussion argues that FP3 approaches a constant-order policy after assuming that the system reaches stationarity.
openItems.scopeBoundary: The conjecture is stronger than the long-lead-time argument. The paper states that the numerical evidence is not a formal proof of close-to-optimality.

source.title: Fixed Non-Stockout-Probability Policies for the Single-Item Lost-Sales Model

openItems.title: Matching lower bounds for nonstationary lost sales with positive lead times
openItems.statement: For nonstationary lost-sales systems with strictly positive lead times, the paper identifies matching lower bounds for its dynamic-regret guarantees as an open question.
openItems.paperEstablishes: The paper develops adaptive algorithms for backlogging and lost-sales systems under piecewise-stationary demand. The positive-lead-time lost-sales guarantee is weaker than the rates obtained for backlogging and zero-lead-time lost sales.
openItems.scopeBoundary: The benchmark is the time-varying optimal base-stock policy. The question does not concern regret relative to the globally optimal dynamic inventory policy.

source.title: Non-Stationary Inventory Control with Lead Times

openItems.title: Demand drift, stochastic lead times, and transient-cost regret
openItems.statement: The paper lists gradually drifting demand and stochastic lead times as extensions and asks whether positive-lead-time regret bounds under transient expected cost can retain the same dependence on the horizon while remaining sublinear in the number of demand regimes when that number is unknown.
openItems.paperEstablishes: The paper studies unknown piecewise-stationary demand, deterministic lead times, and base-stock-policy optimization. It reports guarantees under stationary-average-cost regret and discusses a transient-cost comparison separately.
openItems.scopeBoundary: This item records the extensions named in the paper's conclusion; it does not assert that every stationary inventory theorem fails under nonstationarity.

source.title: Non-Stationary Inventory Control with Lead Times

openItems.title: Sharp constant in the disrupted-mode decentralization condition
openItems.statement: The paper asks whether the sufficient requirement lambda at least a plus 1 can be tightened to lambda at least a plus epsilon-zero for a universal positive constant. It also records a counterexample implying epsilon-zero must exceed 0.25.
openItems.paperEstablishes: The paper proves the Poisson-tail comparison needed for its decentralization criterion under the stated plus-1 condition and uses the result in a multitier inventory network with expediting and disruptions.
openItems.scopeBoundary: The question concerns the constant in the paper's tail comparison and the associated sufficient condition; it is not a general characterization of optimal disruption allocation.

source.title: Managing Multitier Inventory Networks with Expediting Under Normal and Disrupted Modes

statusUpdates.title: Long-lead-time asymptotic optimality of PIL
statusUpdates.summary: van Jaarsveld and Arts prove that PIL dominates the constant-order policy for every finite lead time and is asymptotically optimal as lead time grows for exponentially distributed demand per period. They also establish high-penalty asymptotic optimality under mild distributional assumptions.
statusUpdates.citation: van Jaarsveld and Arts (2024), Operations Research 72(5):1790–1805

statusUpdates.title: PIL guarantees for perishable systems with positive lead times
statusUpdates.summary: Bu, Gong, and Yin establish asymptotic optimality of the best PIL policy as the unit penalty grows for a broad class of unbounded demand distributions in perishable backlogging and lost-sales systems. They also report large-population asymptotic guarantees. The asymptotic regimes stated in the paper are penalty and demand population size, rather than lead time.
statusUpdates.citation: Bu, Gong, and Yin (2026), Management Science, Articles in Advance

statusUpdates.title: Square-root regret under censored demand and positive lead times
statusUpdates.summary: Zhang, Chao, and Shi give an affirmative answer to the rate question posed after Huh et al. (2009): their nonparametric algorithm attains the square-root regret rate relative to the full-information optimal base-stock policy.
statusUpdates.citation: Zhang, Chao, and Shi (2020), Management Science 66(5):1962–1980

statusUpdates.title: A constant-factor guarantee for capped base-stock policies
statusUpdates.summary: A July 2026 working paper proves that the best capped base-stock policy is a 7/3-approximation. The paper describes approximation guarantees for this policy class as previously open and identifies a ratio below 2 as a possible direction for refinement.

literaturePath.policyBenchmark: Single-period newsvendor and a multiperiod inventory model
literaturePath.result: Computes sample-based policies and provides distribution-free sample-size guarantees for near-optimal expected cost.
literaturePath.boundary: This is the sampling-based starting point; it is not the canonical positive-lead-time censored lost-sales model.

literaturePath.policyBenchmark: Best base-stock policy in lost sales with positive lead times
literaturePath.result: Develops a nonparametric adaptive algorithm with a cubic-root convergence rate.
literaturePath.boundary: The benchmark is the best base-stock policy, not the globally optimal dynamic policy.

literaturePath.policyBenchmark: Best base-stock policy in lost sales with positive lead times
literaturePath.result: Attains the square-root regret lower bound with a simulated cycle-update policy.
literaturePath.boundary: The paper closes the rate question for the base-stock benchmark.

literaturePath.result: Shows convergence to a constant-order policy and constructs a sequence that is asymptotically optimal as lead time grows.
literaturePath.boundary: This paper analyzes policy performance rather than learning from historical or censored data.

literaturePath.result: Studies offline pricing and demand learning with censored data and develops near-optimal or minimax-optimal procedures under the paper's identifiable and unidentifiable settings.
literaturePath.boundary: The model allocates a fixed initial inventory through pricing; it does not learn a replenishment policy with positive lead times or a capped base-stock benchmark.

literaturePath.policyBenchmark: Best capped base-stock and best base-stock policies
literaturePath.result: Uses a UCB framework with a Kaplan–Meier estimator; the regret is tight up to a logarithmic factor in the horizon.
literaturePath.boundary: For capped base-stock learning, Remark 5 reports an upper bound with exponential dependence on lead time and attributes it to policy switching. The paper states that this dependence seems inevitable for the capped base-stock system.

literaturePath.result: Provides an exact worst-case analysis for data-driven newsvendor policies under censored observations and examines the roles of Kaplan–Meier estimation and exploration.
literaturePath.boundary: The model is single-period; it does not address positive-lead-time lost-sales replenishment or offline learning of capped base-stock policies.

literaturePath.result: Provides dynamic-regret guarantees for backlogging and lost-sales systems with and without lead times.
literaturePath.boundary: For lost sales with positive lead times, the paper reports weaker rates and explicitly leaves matching lower bounds open.

literaturePath.result: Proves a 7/3 approximation guarantee for the best capped base-stock policy.
literaturePath.boundary: This working paper concerns full-information approximation, not offline statistical estimation or online regret.

literaturePath.policyBenchmark: Best projected-inventory-level and base-stock policies for perishable systems
literaturePath.result: Establishes PIL asymptotic optimality in large-penalty and large-demand-population regimes and compares PIL with base-stock policies across issuance rules.
literaturePath.boundary: The stated asymptotic regimes are penalty and demand population size; the paper does not report long-lead-time asymptotic optimality.
